# Mathlib naming-consistency audit

_Generated by `scripts/naming_audit/naming_audit.py` on 2026-09-16; 239702 declarations in 7463 files scanned._

This is a living document. Every row is identified by its category, declaration/token and file
(not the line number). Re-running the script keeps the `Status` and `Note` cells of rows that are still present,
adds new rows as `open`, and drops rows whose declaration no longer exists. Triage by editing
the `Status`/`Note` cells in place.

Statuses: `open` (not yet looked at), `confirmed` (checked by hand, should be fixed), `fp`
(false positive or accepted exception), `fixed` (renamed; the row disappears on the next run),
`wontfix` (real but deliberately left alone).

Confidence (`conf`) is the scanner's own estimate of how likely a row is a genuine problem; it is
not a triage verdict. Deprecated declarations and `Mathlib/Deprecated/` are excluded everywhere.

## Conventions applied

- Theorems and lemmas: `snake_case`; an `UpperCamelCase` name used inside one becomes
  `lowerCamelCase` (`isCompact_iff_isClosed`), acronyms are lowercased as a block (`ennreal`).
- `Prop`s and `Type`s (structures, classes, inductives, `Prop`/`Type`-valued definitions):
  `UpperCamelCase`. Other definitions (functions, data): `lowerCamelCase`.
- Structure fields follow the same rule as top-level declarations of the same kind.
- Dictionary spellings: `natCast`, `intCast`, `ofNat`, `iSup`/`iInf`, `sSup`/`sInf`,
  `biUnion`, `setOf`, `notMem`, `n + 1` (not `succ`), `ne_zero` (not `nonzero`), …
- A name should describe the statement: `_iff` ↔ `↔`, `_ne_` ↔ `≠`, `_lt_` ↔ `<`, `_inter_` ↔ `∩`.
- The same statement should not exist under two names unless one is an `alias`.

## Findings

### A1: Uppercase tokens in theorem names

Theorem/lemma names are `snake_case`; an `UpperCamelCase` declaration referenced inside one must be written in `lowerCamelCase` (e.g. `isCompact_iff`, not `IsCompact_iff`). Accepted exceptions: single capital letters (`C`, `X`), Greek letters, interval names (`Icc`), and data-valued definitions whose own name is (by exception) `UpperCamelCase` (`Gamma`, `Lp`, `LSeries`). Confidence `high` = the token names an existing `UpperCamelCase` declaration; `low` = short acronym.
